headline: Single-cell and spatial profiling resolves cancer cell states and tumor niches
label: Single Cell Cancer Atlases
summary: Single-cell and spatial atlases are now being paired with bulk cohorts and prognostic signatures to connect cell states with clinical outcome.
synthesis: The dominant thread is single-cell and spatial transcriptomics resolving tumor cell states and microenvironmental niches, linked to clinical behavior. Studies define specific states: an LNM-enriched bladder matCAF population driven by TGF-β1-RUNX2 signaling, gastric neutrophil-epithelial niches arresting B-cell maturation in tertiary lymphoid structures, and an SRGN+ neutrophil–CD8+ T cell axis in glioma myeloid cells. Other work applies pseudotime network analysis to identify a CDK1 betweenness bottleneck in PDAC chemoresistance across a 726k-cell atlas, or combines spatial multi-omics with AI to address heterogeneity-driven target discovery. A recurring new element is linking atlas-scale states to bulk-compatible signatures and external cohorts. Not all items share this framing: RAPPL-Seq, cell-free protein synthesis, cfDNA tissue-of-origin inference, and organoid media comparison address distinct methodological questions, while the breast M2 macrophage signature and ovarian multi-omics study are cohort-level analyses.
